chunks: And Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Himyari narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Abi Basir, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: 'For the owner of this affair, there are four traditions from four prophets: a tradition from Moses, a tradition from Jesus, a tradition from Joseph, and a tradition from Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). As for the tradition from Moses, it is being fearful and awaiting; as for the tradition from Joseph, it is the occultation; as for the tradition from Jesus, it is said: he died, yet he did not die; and as for the tradition from Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), it is the sword.'

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: The owner of the affair (Imam Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What are the four prophetic traditions associated with Imam Mahdi according to Abu Ja'far (AS)?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this hadith to explain the multifaceted nature of the Imam Mahdi’s leadership by linking it to the archetypal experiences of four prophets: Moses’ vigilance, Joseph’s hiddenness, Jesus’ perceived death, and Muhammad’s martial readiness. This synthesis underscores the theological concept that the Imam’s authority encompasses both spiritual concealment and active governance, reflecting a comprehensive model of divine leadership.
